# Agency service configuration

A complete operating workspace for category administration, responsibility routing, original request review and implementation handover. The browser uses the same saved profiles, exact original sources and routing engine as the native command and service adapter.

## Prepare the agency profile

Open **Service configurations** and create or import the complete definition. A configuration contains the agency calendar, categories, departments, roles, groups, staff, message templates, routing rules, source mappings and rollout phases. Save a complete profile version before calculating a routing preview. The working definition can be downloaded independently at any point.

Use an explicit IANA time zone. Resolution dates use the original mapped creation instant and the chosen agency calendar. Calendar days and business days are separate choices. Business weekdays use Sunday 0 through Saturday 6; exclusions are literal YYYY-MM-DD dates. The due result is a date in the declared time zone, with its original creation instant retained.

Categories preserve exact source selectors and reference the responsible department and staff member. Location inclusion and requirement are separate settings. The Other category has its explicit display-order rule. Search keywords are separate from exact source routing. Custom intake fields retain their scope, type, original pointer, choices and optional configured default. A default value is distinguished from an observed source value.

Each staff member has one declared role and explicit group membership. Role and group permissions are represented individually. The operating handover identifies relevant vendor application-order requirements for changing an already-associated role or group, while the proposed configuration remains editable.

## Declare the original source

A source profile specifies a source format, original row-array pointer and row-relative RFC 6901 JSON pointers. Every semantic input is either a pointer into the original row or an explicitly declared literal. Source IDs, categories, status, dates, location and progress wording therefore remain traceable to the original source.

The editor accepts the declared formats:

- Open311 GeoReport v2 response arrays.
- Reviewed follow-through dispatch rows.
- Field destination-update items.
- Other explicitly mapped JSON records.

Open **Original request sources**, choose or paste the complete original JSON and select **Inspect original arrays**. Select the exact original array from the returned structure before retaining the source. The empty pointer selects a root array; /rows selects an object's rows member. The source profile's declared array pointer must equal the selected source array.

The full original file remains downloadable. Search and page through every selected original record; **Open full original** shows the complete row, its original index and JSON pointer. The table's short preview is only a display convenience.

## Route the entire register

Open **Routing and progress** and choose the saved configuration, original source and declared source profile. Save the complete routing preview. Each result carries its source identity, category, department, owner, routes, due-date calculation, public-map decision, source stage, rendered message templates and review issues.

Category selectors use exact typed source equality. An original number, string and null remain distinct. Routing conditions are explicit. Eligibility lists select the applicable categories and source profiles; conditions are combined. Multiple matching routes appear as conflicts rather than an implicit first match.

A routing condition can use a declared semantic input or custom:<field-reference>. The latter reads the selected category's custom field through its declared source pointer, which supports the original custom Location field routing workflow.

A request override changes only the fields explicitly selected in its review. **Prepare override** carries the exact source key into a new routing calculation. Choose the category, responsibility, progress stage or map setting being changed and write the reason. The original source and previous preview remain retained.

Use **Known deployed configuration** to select an exact saved profile version and record who declared it deployed, with its deployment reference. This version is retained for permission and membership migration. An externally supplied deployed definition can be imported and saved separately before selection. Leaving the baseline undeclared keeps the required migration inputs visible in the handover.

Complete preview JSON and routing CSV contain the full result population. Browser paging does not limit the saved calculation or downloads.

## Review progress wording

Template subjects and bodies are rendered from the declared original facts. The template's audience and stage are explicit. Missing selected placeholders appear as unresolved inputs in the preview.

The documented native Comcate merge names are {{issue_number}} and {{case_number}}. The remaining named placeholders are the workspace's handover renderer, with the exact supported names listed in the editor and public source contract. A citizen magic link must be explicitly supplied as a permitted HTTPS URL.

Original closure wording matters. A source can close a case after a citation, administrative disposition or other response. Preserve the actual source status and resolution wording when preparing resident progress; a closure alone does not establish completion of a physical repair.

For resident messages, supply explicit resident wording for responsibility, completion notes and progress summaries under each template. These values are optional when unused; selected placeholders without supplied wording remain unresolved in the preview. The editor retains staff-oriented source facts separately from the approved resident phrasing.

Open **Details and messages** on a routing result to inspect its full calculation and exact rendered staff and resident messages together. The configuration specifies the intended communications for implementation.

## Issue the operating handover

Prepare rollout phases for staff, commissioners or residents with the relevant categories, departments, owner, training items, intake and closure procedures, and entry and exit criteria.

Open **Implementation handovers**, choose the reviewed routing preview and provide the reviewer and notes. The saved handover binds the exact profile version and preview. It carries the configuration, original source context, complete routing results, progress wording and rollout procedure. Download its editable JSON and operating report from the saved handover.

A new profile version requires a corresponding routing preview before its handover. Earlier profiles, previews and releases remain available in their original history.

## Continue and recover

The complete workspace export includes profile versions, source originals, routing previews, releases and completed operations. Open it through **Open a handover** in a new empty workspace to continue the same editable work and retained history.

The browser keeps profile drafts while moving among sections. IndexedDB and local storage retain the newest available draft; the working-definition download also preserves unfinished JSON field text. If another operator saves a newer profile, compare the current version with the retained draft or save that draft as a separate configuration.

Before a workspace mutation is sent, the browser retains its original request ID, expected revision, workspace identity and complete body. After an interrupted response, **Check completion** looks up that same original operation. **Resume saved operation** retries the original body. The receiving operation retains its original identity across the received workspace's identity change.

## Browser/API composition

The static browser consists of index.html, app.mjs, styles.css and browser-assets.json. The local service serves the declared routes and API together.

Writes use application/json and X-Open311-Service-Configuration-Workspace, with requestId and expectedRevision. The browser uses the native profiles, sources, previews, releases and receive operations. Original arrays and full preview populations are read through paged source-rows and preview endpoints, with complete file exports alongside them.

The public SOURCE_CONTRACT.md records the primary product sources, exact supported definition vocabulary and compatibility distinctions. The native source owns the configuration validation, routing rules, due-date calculation, saved history and handover format.

# Municipal service configuration

Service Configuration is a complete operating workbench for the agency settings behind a municipal request service. It saves departments, staff, role and group declarations, service categories, submission fields, routing, resident and staff messages, and an implementation plan. Each saved routing preview applies one exact configuration version to a complete original request register.

The browser, CLI and typed merchant provider open the same private SQLite workspace. Complete editable handovers preserve original source bytes, configuration history, row-level routing choices, rendered messages, declared deployed baselines, implementation releases and original action recovery.

## Operating workflow

1. Retain the original JSON file and select its exact array of requests. Inspect the original fields and map their meanings explicitly.
2. Define the agency, local time zone and due-date calendar. Add departments, named staff, role/group declarations and category responsibility.
3. Configure category selectors, custom submission/location fields, routing conditions, stage-specific message templates and the rollout plan.
4. Save a complete configuration version. Preview the whole selected source using that exact version, with explicit record overrides and any declared deployed baseline.
5. Inspect every unmatched, conflicting or invalid routing result, the original values used in decisions, local due dates, public-map choices and exact message text.
6. Save a named implementation handover from the matching current profile and preview. Export its JSON, printable operating report, full routing CSV and editable workspace.
7. Receive the full workspace into an empty directory and continue the same source and configuration history.

The six-application source selection also includes Open311 collection, reporting, GIS, request/work-order Follow-through and Field Desk. Complete original exports connect these workspaces. [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) describes the maintained installed package; [WORKSPACE.md](WORKSPACE.md) describes the full operator interface.

## Configuration model

| Area | Saved configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Agency | Name, identifier, time zone, calendar/business days, eligible weekdays and holidays |
| Departments and staff | Active departments, named staff, department membership, contact, selected role and groups |
| Permissions | Explicit CRM enablement, administrator and access declarations on named roles/groups |
| Categories | Exact original source selectors, responsibility, keywords, display order, location policy and public-map default |
| Custom fields | Text, number, Boolean, date, single-select and multi-select submission/location fields |
| Routing | Exact typed source/custom-field conditions, eligible categories/sources, responsible staff and collaborators |
| Communication | Staff/resident audience, mapped stage, locale, subject/body and explicit resident-facing wording |
| Source profiles | Original row-array pointer, 23 semantic mappings, native status meanings and public-map mapping |
| Rollout | Named phases, audience, owners, training, entry/exit criteria and notes |

A saved profile is immutable. Editing creates a new version retaining its predecessor. The optional deployed baseline identifies a saved original profile/version and the operator who declared it; migration implications refer to that explicit baseline.

Role and group records preserve declared permissions and the application sequence. The workbench retains those declarations alongside staff assignment and review; the original vendor settings and selected baseline explain the implementation steps.

## Original source and routing semantics

Source inspection lists every original array with its row count and field names. An empty row pointer selects a root array. Mappings use RFC 6901 pointers relative to each original row, or explicit literal JSON values. The source file, original whitespace and UTF-8 byte identity remain available for download.

The mapping vocabulary covers request and issue/case identifiers, service/category/title/description, dates, native status and notes, address/coordinates, resident contact and links, work-order IDs, completion/progress wording and map visibility. It supports Open311 records, Follow-through dispatch rows, Field Desk destination rows and an explicitly mapped register.

Route selectors combine with AND; each declared eligibility list combines its values with OR. Exact JSON scalar types matter. Multiple matching routes remain a visible conflict. A category's valid default responsibility can handle a request with no matching route. Record overrides preserve their original source key and a reason.

Native status values remain part of the original source. Their saved mappings select received, assigned, in-progress, resolved or closed-other stages and an explicit completion meaning. Source dates retain their original values. Due dates use an offset-bearing creation instant, the agency time zone and the selected local calendar; business-day addition uses eligible dates after the local creation date, and zero days retains that date.

Public-map decisions preserve the category default, an explicit typed source-value mapping and any row override. Missing/unrecognized source values produce visible findings according to the saved mapping.

## Messages and implementation releases

Every rendered message retains its original template, audience, stage, recipient, bound values and unresolved tokens. The source issue number is an explicit mapping. Resident-facing assignee, completion and progress wording can be declared separately from internal operating records. Preview messages retain their `deliveryState: 'PREVIEW'` field.

A release binds the exact saved configuration, preview, original source and deployed-baseline declaration. Its complete application stages, remaining requests, migration implications and reviewer notes travel together. Later profile changes require a new matching preview before creating another release.

The format and primary-source rationale are documented in [SOURCE_CONTRACT.md](SOURCE_CONTRACT.md); [SOURCE_REGISTER.json](SOURCE_REGISTER.json) retains source references, and [MODEL_CONTRACT.json](MODEL_CONTRACT.json) names the implemented vocabulary.

## Direct CLI

From the repository root, initialize and open a private directory:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/service-configuration/cli.mjs init \
  --workspace /absolute/private/service-configuration

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/service-configuration/cli.mjs serve \
  --workspace /absolute/private/service-configuration --port 8771
~~~

Run `help` for every command. Mutable commands use the original `--request-id` and observed `--revision`. A repeated exact intent returns its saved result.

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/service-configuration/cli.mjs source-inspect \
  --input /absolute/original/requests.json

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/service-configuration/cli.mjs source-import \
  --workspace /absolute/private/service-configuration \
  --input /absolute/original/requests.json --rows-pointer "" \
  --name "Original service requests" --request-id source-001 --revision 0

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/service-configuration/cli.mjs profile-save \
  --workspace /absolute/private/service-configuration \
  --input /absolute/original/service-definition.json --request-id profile-001 --revision 1
~~~

Use the returned profile ID, profile version and source ID when creating the preview:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/service-configuration/cli.mjs preview-create \
  --workspace /absolute/private/service-configuration \
  --profile-id PROFILE_ID --profile-version PROFILE_VERSION_ID \
  --source-id SOURCE_ID --source-profile SOURCE_MAPPING_ID \
  --name "Complete request routing" --request-id preview-001 --revision 2

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/service-configuration/cli.mjs release-create \
  --workspace /absolute/private/service-configuration \
  --profile-id PROFILE_ID --profile-version PROFILE_VERSION_ID --preview-id PREVIEW_ID \
  --name "Reviewed service implementation" --reviewer "Implementation owner" \
  --request-id release-001 --revision 3
~~~

The revision values above follow a newly initialized sequence. Read `state` for the actual revision when continuing another workspace.

## Exports and receiving

| Kind | Complete saved content |
| --- | --- |
| workspace | Original files, all configuration versions, previews, releases and operation history |
| profile | Selected saved configuration version |
| source | Exact retained original JSON bytes |
| preview-json | Full routing preview with its selected profile, source and baseline |
| preview-csv | Every routing row and its recorded decision fields |
| release-json | Complete reviewed implementation package |
| release-report | Printable operating handover with original choices and rollout |

Exports use create-only output paths. A chosen `--revision` binds an export to the observed workspace edition. Receive the complete workspace into a new empty directory:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/service-configuration/cli.mjs export \
  --workspace /absolute/private/service-configuration --kind workspace \
  --output /absolute/handover/service-workspace.json --revision 4

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/service-configuration/cli.mjs receive \
  --workspace /absolute/private/received-service-configuration \
  --input /absolute/handover/service-workspace.json \
  --request-id receive-service-001 --revision 0
~~~

The received workspace preserves its source UUID and original history, adds the receiving receipt, and remains editable. Unchanged export bytes are stable across process reopen. [MCP.md](MCP.md) provides named host inputs, the 19-tool operating catalog and the typed full-file receiving interface.

# Install municipal service configuration

The **open311-service-configuration** source selection delivers the complete municipal suite: source collection, reporting, GIS, request/work-order Follow-through, Field Desk and service configuration. Each application opens its own saved private directory; full original exports connect them.

## Build the selected source

Use the accepted source commit from the maintained repository:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo . --ref EXACT_ACCEPTED_SOURCE_COMMIT \
  --selection open311-service-configuration \
  --out /absolute/new/service-configuration-package --offline
~~~

Choose a new output directory. The selection carries the original merchant, release store, native installer, Applications and retained-file components. The additive contribution registers the service command, browser assets, four typed exports and source-owned merchant provider.

Direct service modules require Node.js 22.13 or newer with SQLite. The maintained complete merchant runtime requires Node.js 22.16 or newer, Linux, Python 3.11 or newer and util-linux flock. Delivered original sources remain under `package/source`.

| Package export | Interface |
| --- | --- |
| @tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/seller/open311-service-configuration | Configuration, source, routing, calendar, release and workspace types/API |
| @tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/seller/open311-service-configuration/workspace | Durable editable SQLite workspace |
| @tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/open311-service-configuration | Installed merchant provider and original initializer |
| @tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/open311-service-configuration/client | Typed adapter for the existing merchant callTool transport |

## Prepare the original private runtime

Run from the delivered merchant package directory. Select its actual archive and complete SHA-256:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install prepare \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime \
  --archive /absolute/handover/ORIGINAL_MERCHANT_ARCHIVE.tgz \
  --sha256 ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --native --feature schema --feature openapi --feature mcp --operator

npx --no-install starforge runtime-install install \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime

npx --no-install starforge runtime-install inspect \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime --load --source
~~~

Continue an interrupted original installation with `runtime-install resume --dir` and its existing directory. A populated package cache supports `--offline --cache /absolute/private/npm-cache`. Offline native preparation also uses the compiler and Node headers for the selected executable; `--node-headers` identifies the prefix containing `include/node`.

## Initialize or receive the workbench

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  open311-service-configuration init \
  --workspace /absolute/private/service-configuration
~~~

A complete delivered service workspace is received into an empty directory:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  open311-service-configuration receive \
  --workspace /absolute/private/received-service-configuration \
  --input /absolute/handover/service-workspace.json \
  --request-id receive-service-001 --revision 0
~~~

Receiving preserves the original files, all saved profile versions, whole-register previews, declared baselines, implementation handovers and original action history. The database filename is `open311-service-configuration.sqlite`. Select the received directory when opening its application.

## Open Applications

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  open311-service-configuration serve \
  --workspace /absolute/private/service-configuration --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0
~~~

The compact LISTENING record identifies the actual loopback URL, workspace UUID, saved-directory binding and server instance. Open its URL.

In merchant Applications select **Municipal service configuration**, then the same initialized or received directory. The source-owned provider reads the original SQLite identity, binds launch arguments to that directory and verifies the live startup response. Browser draft and interrupted-operation recovery remain bound to the selected directory through receiving.

## Configure and review the whole service

The browser's complete editor covers agency settings, departments and staff, role/group declarations, categories and custom fields, source profiles, routing, templates and rollout. Retain a complete original request file and choose its row array. Save a configuration version, inspect the full resulting routing register, and prepare explicit overrides or resident wording as needed.

A named implementation release keeps the exact profile version, original source, preview, baseline declaration and review together. Its printable handover and JSON preserve remaining requests and the application order. The full editable workspace lets the receiving operator continue the same configuration history.

[MCP.md](MCP.md) supplies private host setup, named source/profile files, paged views and complete file delivery. [WORKSPACE.md](WORKSPACE.md) describes the operator controls. [README.md](README.md) gives source and CLI operations.

## Customer handover

Deliver the full editable workspace JSON, original source, selected configuration, complete routing CSV/JSON, implementation JSON/report and the ordinary operator guide. Keep the accepted installed source identity with that handover. The receiving operator can inspect original decisions, compare declared baseline implications, save the next profile version and build a new source-bound preview.

# Municipal service configuration: source and implementation contract

This module prepares one agency's service categories, staff access declarations, routing, due-date policy, notification wording and phased rollout as a versioned configuration and editable handover. It joins original municipal request records and the existing Follow-through and Field Desk products. A saved profile is a proposed configuration. A release binds a reviewed profile version to the exact imported source and preview used to assess it.

The source register gives the original published guides, their observed HTTP response identities, and the particular facts used below. The accompanying source examples preserve an actual Boston request and identify the containing original response. Entered staffing, calendar and service targets are visibly proposed policy.

## 1. Published behavior and the supported product

Comcate's category guide describes category names and status, optional department, whether a resident may or must supply a location, up to ten single-word keywords, a resolution interval in days, linked email templates and custom fields. Category order is editable; its Other category remains first. Its due-date formula uses creation date plus the category's resolution interval. The guide does not specify a timezone, business-day calendar, holiday set, daylight-saving convention or time of day. This module therefore records the agency's chosen timezone and calendar explicitly. [C131]

The assignment guide uses an Equals comparison against a submission category or a custom location field, followed by a default assignee and collaborators. This module supports that compatibility subset and labels its broader typed selectors as a local configuration model. Keyword suggestions remain separate from reviewed routing. [C241]

Comcate documents roles and groups, one required role per user, CRM enablement, product administrator status and Read-only, Basic and Overwrite access. The group documentation provides optional group membership and permission declarations. The guides do not define a reliable role-versus-group permission precedence algorithm. The role/group restrictions on changing permissions with assigned users are deployment constraints; an internal profile draft remains editable. [C179, C180, C181, C130]

The template guide allows custom email templates with a subject, content and related documents; existing SMS templates can be edited, but custom SMS templates cannot be created. It documents the native merge names {{case_number}} and {{issue_number}}, and a citizen review link. This module prepares email wording and template previews; its other placeholder names are explicitly local handover names. [C184]

An original submission may be closed and reopened. Comcate also documents an optional setting that closes a submission when its code case closes. Neither behavior proves that physical work was completed. Category-level and individual-submission public-map visibility are separately configurable. Anonymous intake depends on the agency's global setting, its Accounts feature and then the category setting. Those dependencies belong in the deployment checklist when used. [C129, C140, C360, C344]

Published customer implementations describe agency-specific categories and ownership, staff communications at workflow stages, and rollout from staff to commissioners and residents. These support a practical configuration, training and handover workflow. They do not establish access to a particular tenant or the chosen agency's service targets. [ATHENS, CONVERSE, VISIBILITY]

## 2. Profile definition

Object IDs are nonempty stable strings and unique within their collection. References use IDs, never display names. Names, descriptions, notes and source labels remain editable. A profile retains its complete definition, version ID, original operation and content identity. Saving a successor creates a new immutable version.

ProfileDefinition:
- name: string
- agency: { id, name, timeZone, calendar: { kind, weekdays, holidays } }
- departments: Department[]
- staff: Staff[]
- roles: Role[]
- groups: Group[]
- categories: Category[]
- templates: Template[]
- routes: Route[]
- sourceProfiles: SourceProfile[]
- rollout: RolloutPhase[]
- note: string

Department = { id, name, active }.

Role and Group = { id, name, description, active, permissions, sourceLabel?, sourceReference? }.
Permissions = { crmEnabled: boolean, crmProductAdmin: boolean, crmAccess: "none" | "read_only" | "basic" | "overwrite" }.
Default permission declaration is false / false / none. Product administrator status or an access level other than none requires crmEnabled. The declaration records intended grants; it does not authenticate an operator or enforce access to a vendor tenant.

Staff = { id, name, departmentIds: string[], roleId: string, groupIds: string[], contact: string, active: boolean }.
A staff entry has exactly one roleId. Group membership is derived from staff.groupIds, avoiding a second independently editable list of members. References must resolve. Active routing targets must be active staff in the selected department. A conflicting role/group declaration is shown for review, without inventing the vendor's grant precedence.

Category = {
  id, sourceSelectors, name, description, active, isOther, displayOrder,
  includeLocation, locationRequired, departmentId, ownerStaffId,
  keywords, resolutionDays, publicMapDefault, customFields, templateIds
}.
sourceSelectors = [{ sourceProfileId, field: "serviceCode" | "category" | "serviceName", value: JSONScalar }].
keywords is an array of at most ten distinct single-word strings. Preserve entered casing, while an implementation may show a separate normalized suggestion key. Keyword suggestions do not select a route.
resolutionDays is null or a nonnegative integer. Null means no configured target. An integer is the entered target, not an inferred provider SLA.
publicMapDefault is "show" or "hide".
locationRequired requires includeLocation. At most one category isOther; when present it is first in displayed order. Duplicate source selectors across applicable categories are a conflict. Do not silently choose the first row or the lowest displayOrder.
CustomField = {
  id, label, kind, scope, required, options, helpText,
  sourcePointer?, defaultValue?
}.
kind = "text" | "number" | "boolean" | "date" | "single_select" | "multi_select".
scope = "submission" | "location".
options = [{ value: string, label: string }].
These field types are this module's neutral schema. Source labels and original values are retained; no assertion is made that they enumerate all native vendor field types.
Select fields require unique option values. Other types have an empty options array. A supplied default must match the declared type; date values are valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD dates. An absent default remains absent.

Template = { id, name, audience, stage, subject, body, locale, active }.
audience = "staff" | "resident".
stage = "received" | "assigned" | "in_progress" | "resolved" | "closed_other".
subject and body are literal text with the allowlisted placeholders in section 6. Rendering escapes the result in the browser; it does not execute HTML, JavaScript or arbitrary expressions.

Route = {
  id, name, active, categoryIds, sourceProfileIds, selectors,
  departmentId, ownerStaffId, collaboratorStaffIds, templateIds, note
}.
selectors = [{ field: string, operator: "equals", value: JSONScalar }
           | { field: string, operator: "in", values: JSONScalar[] }].
The field names resolve through an explicit semantic mapping or custom:<categoryFieldId>. Submission-category and custom-location selectors identify their scope in the profile. A custom location field used by a Comcate-compatible rule must reference an actual declared field with scope location.
There is no implicit rule priority. Match behavior is defined in section 4.

SourceProfile = {
  id, name, kind, rowsPointer, mapping, statusMappings,
  publicMapOverrideMapping?, note
}.
kind = "open311_georeport_v2" | "follow_through_dispatch_v1"
     | "field_destination_update_v1" | "mapped_records".
mapping is a keyed object of semantic fields to exactly one of { pointer: string } or { literal: JSONValue }.
statusMappings = [{ sourceValue: JSONScalar, stage, completionMeaning: string }].
publicMapOverrideMapping = {
  values: [{ sourceValue: JSONScalar, publicMap: "show" | "hide" | "default" }]
}.
Its input is the value resolved by mapping.publicMapOverride; the override declaration does not carry another pointer.
A mapping's pointer is a JSON Pointer relative to one selected original row. A rowsPointer is relative to the imported complete JSON document. Pointer decoding follows the ~0 / ~1 escaping rules and own object members; there is no evaluation of expressions. An empty pointer selects the complete value. Missing pointer, null, empty string and literal value remain distinct.
A literal is an entered mapping choice and is labeled as such, rather than attributed to the original source.
Status mappings match exact typed values, preserve the original status and notes, and express the operator's intended communication stage. Duplicate sourceValue mappings conflict.
Each public-map sourceValue must appear once; section 7 defines explicit default, absent and unknown values.

RolloutPhase = {
  id, name, audience: "staff" | "commissioners" | "resident",
  categoryIds, departmentIds, ownerStaffId,
  trainingItems: string[], entryCriteria: string[], exitCriteria: string[], note
}.
Rollout order is the array order. It records named owners, actual audiences, training and measurable acceptance criteria.

The agency calendar is { kind: "calendar_days" | "business_days", weekdays: number[], holidays: string[] }.
timeZone is an explicit IANA timezone. Weekdays use Sunday=0 through Saturday=6. Holidays are explicit valid YYYY-MM-DD local dates. A business-day calendar requires at least one weekday. A calendar-day policy ignores weekday/holiday exclusions for arithmetic while retaining them as declared configuration.

## 3. Source profiles and exact upstream seams

A source import retains the complete original file bytes, filename/content type when available, SHA-256, original URL/capture metadata, chosen profile and row location. An imported subset is labeled a subset with its original containing-response identity and selected rows. An example row does not establish the completeness of a city-wide cohort.

Open311:
- rowsPointer "" for a response array.
- requestId <- /service_request_id
- issueNumber <- /service_request_id when the selected template needs {{issue_number}}
- serviceCode <- /service_code
- serviceName <- /service_name
- status <- /status
- statusNotes <- /status_notes
- createdAt <- /requested_datetime
- updatedAt <- /updated_datetime
- address <- /address
- map values, case IDs and citizen links require explicit mappings when present.

Follow-through:
- schema commons.open311.follow-through-dispatch.v1; rowsPointer /rows.
- Each dispatch row has key, serviceRequestId, sourceSha256, request, orders, work, geometry and mapped.
- request contains the original normalized request and its untouched source object. orders contains approved linked orders; work is the approved local work record.
- A complete follow-through workspace has schema commons.open311.follow-through-workspace.v1 and records of {kind,id,value}. Select and validate the intended dispatch record explicitly before using the dispatch profile.
- Source request status and the approved dispatch action remain different fields. Entered routing and due dates cannot rewrite either source.

Field Desk:
- schema commons.open311.field-destination-update.v1; rowsPointer /items.
- The complete update contains id, name, workspaceId, workspaceRevision, createdAt, reviewer, destination, note, items, attachments, totals and sha256.
- Each item retains its visit, original sourceRow, source/approval references, crew and dispatch definition.
- A field visit completion or request_closure destination action is a reviewed local action. The original external request status is retained until an actual provider result changes it.
- Service mapping is explicit through the item's retained sourceRow/request or operator-reviewed destination fields. The adapter must not assume a /rows array or flatten away original approval/source identity.

Mapped records:
- A complete arbitrary JSON array/object can be used with rowsPointer and explicit mappings.
- Dates are accepted only under the declared mapping and date interpretation. A string such as 10/08/2026 is not parsed by guessing whether it is month-first or day-first.
- IDs are retained as original strings/numbers. Converting a numeric identifier requires exact representability; unsafe JavaScript integers produce an input diagnostic.
- Original pointer values and source identity remain available beside the configured interpretation.

The supported mapping keys are requestId, serviceCode, category, serviceName, title, description, createdAt, updatedAt, closedAt, status, statusNotes, address, latitude, longitude, residentEmail, trackingUrl, publicMapOverride, issueNumber, caseNumber, workOrderIds, completionNote, progressSummary and magicLink. Selectors for declared category custom fields use custom:<categoryFieldId>. There are no compatibility aliases for earlier draft mapping names. The {{issue_number}} token resolves only from issueNumber; requestId is not an implicit fallback.

## 4. Deterministic category, route and ownership preview

1. Resolve the selected source profile and preserve each original row.
2. Evaluate exact category selectors applicable to that source profile. An active category may match on serviceCode, category or serviceName; two matching categories are a conflict.
3. Evaluate each active route's eligibility. Values within categoryIds and within sourceProfileIds use OR; an empty list explicitly means all. Both eligibility dimensions and every selector within a route must match.
4. Selector comparisons preserve JSON type. "2" and 2 differ. equals has one value; in has a nonempty list. No substring, fuzzy match, coercion or rule-order tie breaker is applied.
5. A single matching route produces proposed department, assignee and collaborators with the route ID as its basis. With zero matching routes, an identified category's valid recorded defaults may be shown with basis CATEGORY_DEFAULT. Otherwise assignment remains unresolved.
6. Two or more matching routes produce a conflict even when their owners happen to match. The operator can narrow or remove a selector and create another profile version.
7. Resolve every referenced active staff, department, collaborator and template. Invalid ownership or missing required field is a row diagnostic, not a silent fallback.

The Comcate-compatible export subset is Equals against submission category or a custom location field, plus default assignee and collaborators. Local in conditions and other semantic fields appear as proposed rule requirements in handover, not as invented native API payloads.

A planned assignee is visibly a proposed routing result. An "assigned" or progress notification preview states its configured action basis; it is not proof that an external work-order assignment occurred. Reassignment, source status and local approved actions remain separately inspectable.

## 5. Due-date arithmetic

For an offset-bearing creation instant, convert it to the configured agency timezone and take the resulting local Gregorian date. Add the category's configured number of days to that civil date, not to an epoch by multiples of 86,400 seconds.

- calendar_days: increment the date by the specified number of calendar days.
- business_days: increment one date at a time after the creation date and count only selected weekdays that are not in the explicit holiday set.
- zero days: return the creation local date without rolling it to a business day.
- null target: retain dueDate null with basis NO_TARGET.
- Missing, invalid or timezone-ambiguous source date: retain the original value and expose an unresolved date diagnostic.
- A date-only source can be used only by an explicit date-only mapping policy; it is already a local date and must not be silently treated as UTC midnight.
- Daylight-saving transitions do not add or remove a civil day. The output is a date-only target, not an invented deadline instant or hour.

A preview retains source creation value, interpreted creation local date, timezone, calendar, interval, computed date and profile version. An imported source expected_datetime remains original data; it is not overwritten by the proposed target. Any comparison labels both values and their independent bases.

The supplied Boston record was created at 2026-10-08T11:28:01Z. Under the explicitly proposed America/New_York policy this is October 8. A proposed two-calendar-day target is October 10; a proposed two-business-day target with Monday–Friday and no holidays is October 12. These are examples of this profile's chosen policy.

## 6. Template allowlist and honest progress wording

The exact local token allowlist is:

{{agency_name}}, {{issue_number}}, {{case_number}}, {{service_category}},
{{department_name}}, {{assignee_name}}, {{request_created_date}},
{{request_updated_date}}, {{due_date}}, {{source_status}},
{{source_status_notes}}, {{location}}, {{work_order_ids}},
{{completion_note}}, {{progress_summary}}, {{magic_link}}.

Only {{issue_number}} and {{case_number}} are documented here as Comcate native merge names. Every other name is part of this module's rendered preview/handover. A vendor deployment task maps it to the tenant's actual supported field or renders the desired fixed content.

Use explicit semantic values and the selected profile. Do not evaluate dot paths, loops, expressions or arbitrary object keys inside templates. A missing selected token remains visibly unresolved with its token name; it is not replaced by an empty string. Preserve the exact template, resolved values, unresolved set, source row, profile version and rendered result.

magic_link requires a source-mapped or explicitly entered permitted HTTPS citizen-review URL. Do not construct a link to a staff session or internal engineering location. It remains unresolved when no suitable original URL exists.

Staff-only owner notes and internal progress values do not become resident wording automatically. A resident-facing template uses explicitly supplied public wording and selected public source values. Assignment, completion and closure statements retain their action/source basis. A preview never creates an actual sent-email event; actual provider sending and readback would be a separately implemented transport.

The original Boston example has status "closed" with notes "Resolved. Citation issued. - Property has been cited." Its proposed mapping uses stage closed_other and retains that literal disposition. Neither the template nor the category should change the statement into "the trash was removed" or infer a repaired asset.

The guides describe attachments in email management and related template documents. The current profile DTO does not introduce a new attachment transport. Existing original source/Field Desk attachment identities can be referenced in the operator's handover and deployed through an actual supported integration.

## 7. Public-map and anonymous-intake settings

Category publicMapDefault supplies the proposed default. When publicMapOverrideMapping is configured, the original per-request value is read through mapping.publicMapOverride and compared with its values array of {sourceValue,publicMap} entries.

- Missing or null override means inherit the category default.
- A recognized show/hide entry records the original value and chosen override.
- A recognized default entry explicitly inherits the category default and retains that basis.
- An unrecognized non-null value is a visibility diagnostic.
- Duplicate sourceValue entries are a profile error.
- A request lacking a resolved category has unresolved default visibility.

A visibility preview lists the original reference, resolved visibility and its basis. It does not publish the complete raw source object, names, addresses or internal notes by default. Any later public-map publication must use an explicitly selected display-field mapping and the receiving system's actual behavior.

The published anonymous-intake dependency is retained as a deployment requirement when relevant: agency Accounts enabled, global anonymous allowance, then the category allowance. This initial DTO does not claim to provision those live settings; handover records their actual receiving-system values and any remaining configuration action.

## 8. Prior deployed profile, migration and rollout

An internal draft can change roles, groups, users and permissions. Its predecessor and changes remain available. The vendor restriction applies when editing a role or group already associated with users in a deployed tenant.

When comparing to a known deployed baseline, include a migration table with the exact affected IDs, old/new permissions, assigned users and proposed sequence:
1. Create a replacement role/group with the reviewed target permissions, or schedule a detach/edit/reattach sequence.
2. Reassign affected users through the actual supported user/membership workflow.
3. Verify their intended access declarations and active operational ownership.
4. Retire the superseded declaration only after the reassignment is complete.

The plan records the chosen sequence and reviewer. A profile save does not execute it. If the deployed baseline or memberships are unavailable, mark those particular migration inputs unresolved and still retain the complete editable target profile. Do not fabricate current users or turn that unknown into a blanket prohibition on draft engineering.

A rollout phase includes named owner, categories/departments, audience, training items, entry criteria and exit criteria. A practical sequence is staff preparation and operating walkthrough, limited commissioner use where appropriate, then resident rollout. This is an adjustable plan based on the published adoption example, not a requirement that every agency has a commissioner pilot.

The complete handover includes:
- editable agency profile and all immutable versions used by releases;
- original imported source files and their metadata/identity;
- full preview rows, diagnostics, matched rule/category and ownership basis;
- date-policy inputs and computed targets;
- exact templates and rendered/unresolved outputs;
- public-map decisions and migration/apply-order tasks;
- rollout training and acceptance records;
- complete exports and operation history for independent receiving.

## 9. Storage and transport join

The agreed route families are state, profiles, sources, previews and releases. Profile/source writes and release construction retain requestId and expectedRevision. Source and profile IDs in a preview identify immutable versions. Changing a draft cannot silently mutate an existing preview or release.

A preview offers paginated rows for the browser and a complete downloadable result. Summary counts include original rows, matched/unmatched categories, unique/conflicting/unassigned routes, unresolved dates/tokens and visibility diagnostics. A release binds its exact preview, definition/source identities and operator review; any unresolved required migration or input is enumerated in the receiving handover.

A complete source import and full export keep the original bytes and history together. Independent receiving validates the envelope, identities and references before reopening the same editable product. Existing request/source identity is not changed by category names, staff display names, new notifications or configured date targets.
